Maya —

Appreciate the sample — that makes it concrete. Quick summary up front, then Kim will follow up with the formal language for procurement.

Short answer: we amortize static prefixes across calls when the prefix is stable and re-used (prefix amortization), but we also apply per-request rounding for final invoice line items. The reconciliation steps are:
- Track per-session prefix fingerprinting (we detect identical prefix hashes across calls).
- Compute amortized prefix cost as (prefix_tokens * prefix_weight) distributed across calls that reused it in the billing window.
- After amortization, requests are bucketed into our token-bands for rounding (we call them "bands" rather than single-token minima). Discounts are applied at the invoice line level after aggregation, not pre-rounding per individual microscopic call.

Hi Maya / Jordan —

Thanks for the sample. I’ve attached a short worked example (see billing_walkthrough_jb.xlsx) — below is the procurement-friendly explanation you can drop into the SOW.

Procurement summary for SOW (plain language):
- Prefix amortization: If multiple requests in a given billing window (30-day default) reuse the same static prefix (identical prefix hash), Redwood allocates the prefix token cost proportionally across those requests rather than charging the full prefix each time. This reduces charges when customers reuse large context blobs.
- Rounding & bands: After amortization, tokens are aggregated per-request and then coalesced into discrete billing bands. Our bands are 100-token granularity for the hosted SKU (example: 1-100 => billed as 100; 101-200 => billed as 200). This is intended to balance invoicing clarity with anti-abuse protection.
- Minimum effective floor vs. billing quantum: We do not currently have a "per-call $ minimum" across the board; instead we enforce banding quantums. For very high-frequency microcalls (e.g., many single-token generations), amortization will reduce the effective per-call charge because the heavy prefix cost is distributed; however each call is still bucketed into the nearest band for final line-itemization.
- Discount application: Discounts tied to committed volume are applied to the aggregated billed tokens for the invoice period (after amortization and banding). Practically: compute amortized tokens per call => sum across invoice period => apply contract discount => invoice. This prevents discount manipulation by splitting calls.

Worked numeric example (from spreadsheet):
- Prefix = 50,000 tokens; reused by 10,000 calls in month => amortized prefix per call = 5 tokens.
- Typical call generates 20 tokens => per-call pre-band tokens = 25 tokens (20 + 5).
- Banding to 100-token quantum => each call billed as 100 tokens.
- Aggregated billed tokens for month = 100 * 10,000 = 1,000,000 tokens.
- Contract discount = 20% on monthly billed tokens => discount applies to the 1,000,000 aggregated tokens.

Edge-case notes (short):
- Streaming sessions with continuously appending prefixes: we fingerprint rolling windows; if the prefix changes more often than the billing window, amortization will be lower.
- Function/tool-calls that mutate context: when the server alters the prefix blob, amortization is reset for the fingerprinted segment.
- Anti-abuse: we reserve the right to enforce rate-limited minimum bands for accounts under trial/promo to prevent microcall spam.
